stories.title: Proton's CTO tells engineers "Your old job is gone": the job is now directing AI agents, and the next step is rebuilding the whole development process
stories.one_liner: Proton published an internal memo by CTO Bart Butler arguing that writing code by hand is no longer the engineer's core job.
stories.summary: Proton published an internal memo by CTO Bart Butler, written about a month earlier for its engineers. It says writing great code manually is "a core skill whose time has passed" and that every engineer is now "a team leader, a manager" whose direct reports are the models and agents they use: their job is to help the LLM write better code faster, step in where it cannot, and improve shared context files, skills and prompts so it needs less babysitting. Butler stresses this is "not the death of expertise" nor of good engineering practices, though some rules, such as how many tests are worth writing, will change as costs fall. He says Proton has been stuck in "phase 1", using LLMs to speed up existing workflows, which is why productivity has not jumped; "phase 2" means removing the bottlenecks that appear elsewhere, such as CI, design, approvals and code review, and he expects most human code review to end. He calls falling behind "an existential threat to the success of the mission itself" and says it is past time for Proton to commit as an organisation.
stories.eli5: Engineers used to build everything brick by brick. Now AI helpers lay the bricks fast, and the engineer's job is to lead them, fix their mistakes and teach them to need less help.
stories.why_it_matters: A CTO, at a privacy-first company, is telling his own engineers in writing that the bottleneck is no longer typing code but the review, CI and approval process around it.
stories.spotlight_reason: It fits a clear pattern this month: an Anthropic hiring manager dropped coding interviews because Claude now does them better (28 Oct); Microsoft's Copilot Cowork team merged 1,211 pull requests in one day, mostly written by agents (2 Nov); and Microsoft's David Fowler ran about 90 agent-written pull requests for ASP.NET Core in a day (Context Window, 2 Nov). Proton now says the same thing from the management side.

stories.title: CrossSWE benchmark tests coding agents on changes that span several repositories
stories.one_liner: Researchers introduced CrossSWE, a new benchmark for cross-repository joint development, to test coding agents on multi-repository tasks.
stories.summary: Real-world software development often spans multiple interdependent repositories. To test coding agents on these tasks, researchers introduced CrossSWE. This benchmark comprises 171 real-world instances spanning 165 repositories, 20 technical domains, and 13 programming languages. It verifies the necessity of coordinated changes by testing whether partial repository modifications are insufficient to achieve the intended behavior. An evaluation of five large language models showed substantial challenges. The strongest model, GPT-6.1 Sol, achieved only 58.48% Pass@1. Furthermore, cross-repository inconsistencies emerged as the most prevalent failure mode at 44.2%.
stories.eli5: It is like trying to build a toy house where the pieces come from different boxes, and you have to make sure they all fit together properly.
stories.why_it_matters: Multi-repository software engineering tasks remain difficult for current large language models, highlighting the need to improve coordination across interdependent codebases.

stories.title: Balanov Releases Uncut, a Lossless and Headless Coding Agent Harness
stories.one_liner: Uncut is a tiny, lossless, headless coding agent harness packaged as a 7 MB static Go binary with four tools.
stories.summary: Balanov released Uncut, a tiny coding agent harness for shell pipelines, CI jobs, containers, and agent experiments. The tool consists of a 7 MB static Go binary with four tools and plain stdin and stdout. It features no TUI, telemetry, plugin system, background agents, automatic retries, or context compaction. Uncut sends the entire conversation on every model call without truncating file contents or combined command output. It exits with an error if a provider cuts a response at its output limit. It supports Linux, macOS, and Windows for amd64 and arm64 architectures under the MIT license.

stories.title: Anthropic releases FlashProve for cryptographic proofs that a model really ran
stories.one_liner: Anthropic released FlashProve, an open-source system using zkSNARKs to generate cryptographic proofs verifying that specific AI models produced given responses.
stories.summary: Anthropic released FlashProve, a system for provable inference using a cryptographic proof type known as a zkSNARK. The system lets a model provider commit to a model and prove that each response came from that model without revealing the private weights. For a 400 billion parameter mixture of experts model, a single H100 GPU generates proofs at around 110 tokens per second with a proof size of about 19 megabytes per 1,024-token request. Anthropic released code, documentation, and Lean proofs under the Apache 2.0 license to allow other teams to inspect and improve the work.
stories.eli5: It is like having a special seal on a letter that proves exactly which writer penned it without letting anyone read the secret recipe used to write it.
stories.why_it_matters: Cryptographic proofs enable users and independent evaluators to verify that AI responses actually come from the requested models.
stories.spotlight_reason: It applies zero-knowledge cryptographic proofs to LLM inference, creating a new method to verifiably prove an output came from a specific model.

new_terms.definition: A goal that enables a user with limited computational resources and without information about weights to verify that a response came from a requested model.

stories.title: Yandex Research's FLAMIA brings microscaling attention kernels to NVIDIA Blackwell
stories.one_liner: FLAMIA is a family of attention kernels for NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs that speeds up Transformer training using MXFP8 and mixed NVFP4/FP8 paths.
stories.summary: Attention remains a high computational cost in Transformer training, especially at long context lengths. NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs offer high-throughput low-precision matrix multiplication, but using it requires addressing quantization overhead and other issues. Researchers presented FLAMIA, a family of attention kernels for Blackwell with MXFP8 and mixed NVFP4/FP8 training paths. The design combines token-block scaling, safeguards against leakage, and consistent forward and backward computations. The MXFP8 path accelerates the combined forward and backward attention call by factors of 1.10 to 1.40 times on B200 and 1.06 to 1.42 times on B300. Training stability and quality preservation were validated on Llama-style models.
stories.eli5: This method reorganizes how an AI processes long blocks of text so it can use special fast hardware math without breaking anything.
stories.why_it_matters: Low-bit hardware throughput translates into practical attention acceleration when quantization, training numerics, and document scheduling are jointly designed.

new_terms.definition: A design that reuses quantized operands across matrix orientations.
A scheduling approach that supports variable-length documents directly in packed layouts without repacking.

stories.title: Octomind releases an open-source coding agent harness written in Rust

It allows any language model to work in a repository through MCP, supporting interactive use, stdin pipes, daemons, WebSockets, and editor agents. On 25 benchmark tasks from merged pull requests, it solved 24.

new_terms.definition: Learning compression folds older turns into a summary that cites content-addressed blocks while raw messages stay in a per-session archive.

stories.title: Encrypted firmware on Nvidia's RTX Spark laptops slows AI inference on Linux, report says
stories.one_liner: Running native Linux on Nvidia RTX Spark laptops locks the GPU clock speed when plugged in, drastically slowing AI inference.
stories.summary: Laptops running on the Nvidia RTX Spark platform experience severe performance drops when using native Linux while plugged into wall power. A hidden Windows-only component named Nvidia Platform Controllers and Framework manages power delivery, but its power table is encrypted and lacks a Linux equivalent. This causes the GPU clock speed to collapse to roughly 780 MHz instead of hitting over 2 GHz, reducing inference speeds significantly. Developers can bypass this limitation by using the Windows Subsystem for Linux, which maintains full GPU boost performance.

stories.title: CloudOpsBench finds reasoning is the bottleneck for AI agents running cloud operations
stories.one_liner: A new open-source benchmark called CloudOpsBench reveals that reasoning is the biggest bottleneck for AI agents handling cloud DevOps tasks.
stories.summary: CloudOpsBench is a new open-source benchmark built by experienced DevOps engineers. It measures how well AI agents handle typical DevOps tasks in the cloud, including fixing services, removing resources, restricting access rights, rolling out updates, and decommissioning projects. Version 1.0 includes 45 tasks on AWS. Even the best models fail at many tasks. Claude Fable 5.1 solved 60 percent, while GPT-6 Astra managed 53 percent. According to a team led by Ang Chen at the University of Michigan, the main problem is reasoning rather than a lack of knowledge. About 80 percent of failures happen because agents misjudge task scope, miss relevant services, or stop too early.
stories.eli5: AI agents are like little robot helpers trying to tidy up a giant digital toy room. Even the smart ones struggle to figure out the right steps to clean up the whole room without stopping too early.
stories.why_it_matters: Fixing cloud operations requires improving AI reasoning rather than just adding more knowledge.
